Virginia Feito on the Film Adaptation of Her Novel ‘Victorian Psycho’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication.
  • I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The writer is the lowest form of life on a movie.- Martin McDonagh.

Recent findings suggest that when I finished editing my second novel, Victorian Psycho, I could not imagine we would be shooting the film adaptation the following year, mere months after the book’s publication. Generally, making a movie is one big miracle produced by an amalgamation of thousands of other tiny miracles. But when I met Zach Wigon, I understood that this was a joyfully tenacious person who was going to make this movie if it cost him his life.

I decided then to undertake this journey that would take me metaphorically to Hollywood but geographically to a county just outside of Dublin, where we would recreate the Ensor House of my novel. Among film stars, an Irish crew, and (rumored) ticks, the adaptation of Victorian Psycho—based on my screenplay, which is based on my novel, which is based on my ego, I guess—was born. Throughout the shoot I kept a sort of pseudo diary in order to remember every surreal detail from which I still haven’t recovered. I’ve chosen to reproduce some of it here.

Industry observers note that director Zach Wigon and producer Lisa Kelly call me from the set on the first day of shooting (Zach and I have agreed I won’t visit the set until after the first week so the cast and crew can acclimate without me hovering over them, because I am an intense fame whore, and also, I suppose, to signal I’m not crucial enough to pull a P.L. Travers and attempt to boycott the movie).

Over the phone, the producer notes she can’t wait to meet in person. I tell her I’m underwhelming.

It has been revealed that they promise to send me the dailies. I spend all day waiting for the dailies. The dailies never come.

It has been revealed that at around 9 p.m., I spiral because I don’t know whether to celebrate with Champagne or KFC. I decide to have both.

I finally get the dailies. I fall in love with Maika Monroe’s character so hard it’s like I have an obsessive crush circa 2006 whose Facebook photos I’m compulsively looking at. But in this case it’s the same scene throughout five almost identical takes of Maika calling a 10-year-old boy a little idiot.

Industry observers note that over the phone, Zach mentions concerns about a specific scene because we don’t have the budget for that many extras. I get carried away and suggest shipping over a whole battalion of free extras from Spain because, in my head, it’s going to be me and my friends, drunk and decked out in period clothing like we’re at a cheesy bachelorette party. One friend starts making childcare arrangements and another cancels her Holter monitor appointment so she can come to the shoot. What could go wrong?

I start to realize what could go wrong.

According to recent reports, I am informed we are probably no longer going to need the extras, and I feel a huge wave of relief as I uninvite my excited friends. I pack a suitcase for Ireland. It weighs 57 pounds.

I have a steak on the plane to Dublin at, like, 3 p.m., because when you’re flying business and somebody offers you steak, you take it.

The hotel room is wonderful, but I jokingly tell Zach over the phone that it’s on a first floor, so someone might crawl up and break in through the window and rape me, and he laughs at first but then is concerned and tells me to request a room on a higher floor, and I tell him it was a joke, but it wasn’t really.

I fill up the hotel room bathtub and call reception for a glass of red wine because I am a queen and I am queening. The glass doesn’t come, so in my anxious impatience I attempt to open a bottle of red wine sitting above the minibar. The cork crumbles because I’ve never understood how to use a corkscrew—like the compass in math class, I just faked my way through it my entire life and hoped for the best. So I call reception for another glass of red wine. They bring me all the glasses of wine and also properly uncork the bottle, and I watch Seinfeld in the bathtub while I drink red wine. I get drunk and paint my nails.

I arrive on set slightly Bromazepamed. It is extremely surreal to exist in a set labeled “Mr. Pounds’s Bedroom.” I am used to living in the fictional world inside my head but not used to it becoming more real than real life itself.

Maika hugs me when we meet, and I swallow a sob and refrain from smelling her hair (partly because it is, in fact, a wig). Everyone on set appears so happy to meet me, I suspect a Good Bye, Lenin! situation in which I have been diagnosed with cancer and for some reason the cast and crew all know but I don’t know. This isn’t the plot of Good Bye, Lenin!, but you’ll know what I mean if you’ve seen it.

Zach asks me to read the VOs in every scene, which means I’m in the scene with Ruth Wilson, Jason Isaacs, and Maika, and I’m about to have a stroke.

Jason eats for real in every single take and has already gulped down seven sausage rolls, so if I fuck up my VO, I will kill myself.

Suddenly experiencing fiction collectively feels very superior to experiencing it privately. This does not bode well for the rest of my career as a novelist.

According to recent reports, there is a scene in a cramped drawing room in which I must read the VO, but I’m supposed to hide from the camera, so I crawl on all fours behind an antique couch and grovel my way around the room while the boom op steps on my hands. I secretly think the boom op hates me because I’m always in his way and have an irritating habit of apologizing when he slams into me.

I start developing Irish inflections, so I say it, “I start developing Irish inflections,” but the Irish seem happy about it, so I pursue it.

In a recent development, jason Isaacs starts doing card tricks between takes because Jason Isaacs is actually magic and also indefatigable. Only one thing could ever defeat Jason Isaacs, and it’s the ghost allegedly living on the third floor.

Even though Zach asked me to oversee the second unit, I don’t think anyone believes I’m actually going to do this—and between you and me, I don’t really even know what a second unit is. It doesn’t help I can’t concentrate on what we’re shooting because we’re in the middle of the woods and someone said there were ticks, so I’m wrapping Sellotape around my ankles, hoping this way they won’t be able to crawl up my legs.

According to recent reports, like your worst trauma, I insert myself into the movie forever via a small cameo. I literally just have to stand in a wig while I smile and nod, but I do it in such a way that I ruin every single take. “Just smile…like a normal person,” the second-unit director says. I reason Zach can just cut me out of the movie, and I will only have wasted everybody’s time and money. There are worse things, like smiling normally but having no cameo. I cope by chewing on another Bromazepam and another chocolate bar. (Every morning I take the chocolate bar from the hotel minibar. It will invariably become an asset in the long afternoons on set, kind of like in prison or high school.).

I change hotel rooms because I have developed an intense FOMO with which I’m always fearing there is a better hotel room for the same price somewhere in the vicinity. This FOMO is also rampant on set between the different units—in the first unit, you have the cinematographer, Nico Aguilar, laughing in the sunlight, talking about color palettes, while in the second unit, we’re shooting clocks and screaming at each other because we still have 17 establishing shots to go.

In a recent development, anyway, I change hotel rooms, and the latest room is so superior to my previous room it’s like an entirely new hotel. I consider changing hotel rooms further. Perhaps I can somehow upgrade my way into a presidential suite.

It has been revealed that my parents visit the set. My dad peers over his glasses at the fake lobster cake, and when I tell him the toilets are in trailers, he sighs gravely.

Industry observers note that jason Isaacs convinces my dad to take up tennis again even though my dad’s not supposed to play tennis after his seven hernias. But my dad is so inspired by this actor, who is not a doctor but whose performance in The Patriot my dad can’t help but praise at least once a month, that he will immediately start playing tennis again upon his return to Spain, and whatever medical problems arise henceforth shall all be Jason Isaacs’s fault.

At the Shelbourne restaurant that night, my mom tells the sommelier how she can’t drink red wine anymore because it makes her anxious, and he kneels on the floor beside her and places a hand on his heart as if she were confiding something intimate to him like her fear of death.

Suddenly, real life feels less real than fictional life.

Industry observers note that obama is visiting Dublin and he’s booked the entire floor, so he essentially kicks me out of the Shelbourne (probably to stay in the JFK Suite next door to my room, which is disappointingly predictable), so I go to The Hoxton, because what is life if you’re not constantly changing hotel rooms? The Hoxton is really lovely, but I get OCD about the light bulbs in the room because they appear mismatched, so I ask housekeeping to change them, but they claim not to have any extra light bulbs, which sounds suspect—like, what do they do if a light bulb suddenly goes out? Do they just never replace it?

Sources indicate that we end the shoot at 5 a.m. I am wearing a thick puffer coat and a thermal T-shirt and a furry hat, plus fur-lined boots over my Sellotaped ankles, although I wonder, If ticks can survive this temperature, they kind of deserve to live off my blood. Nobody else seems as concerned about the cold as me, but then again, most of them are Irish.

Sadly, when we wrap, we are all so exhausted everyone races to clean up and leave, and it is sort of anticlimactic. I don’t know what I was expecting, but balloons falling from the skies did flash through my mind.

In the car on the way to our respective quarters, Zach and I look out the window, wide-eyed, like kidnapped children. Zach starts discussing a fresh project for us. I wonder if he is a sociopath.

I type this over a year later, sitting at my desk in Madrid, striving to work on my next novel. I feel empty inside knowing there is no car to pick me up and take me to set and thereby escape reality for extended periods of time, until set becomes reality and reality becomes a limbo in which you wait for noted reality.

I am working on a novel, but also on four new scripts. I hope to return to reality someday.

This story was originally published in Vanity Fair España.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, “[Jonathan Zuch] is such a genius,” gushes Cal as he sets up a JoySystem in Jason’s living room.
  • According to recent reports, jason, ever-stoic, doesn’t seem fully convinced, mostly going along with things for the enjoyment of spending time with his buddy.
  • Recent findings suggest that like most in-universe media in GTA VI, Tenebrae LuxÂ is a giant, heaving mass of satire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6.

In a recent development, “[Jonathan Zuch] is such a genius,” gushes Cal as he sets up a JoySystem in Jason’s living room. “He’d love to work with other people, but he’s too fuckin’ good at everything. It’d just slow him down. You know, the time it takes him to explain something, he could just make shit quicker. You can see it on the screen, man, it’s so fuckin’ raw.”.

According to recent reports, jason, ever-stoic, doesn’t seem fully convinced, mostly going along with things for the enjoyment of spending time with his buddy. I wasn’t really convinced either when GTA VI forced me into the short intro of Tenebrae Lux. But despite the entire thing mostly existing as a completely unsubtle barb directed at one indie game auteur in particular, Tenebrae LuxÂ hooked me immediately by showing off a series of surprisingly mind-bending puzzles. While some (Cal) might expect such things from a genius like Zuch, I wasn’t at all prepared to bust out my puzzle notebook while playing Grand Theft Auto VI!

Recent findings suggest that like most in-universe media in GTA VI, Tenebrae LuxÂ is a giant, heaving mass of satire. Rendered in black and white and dripping with angst, it follows a Man Who Won’t Shut The Fuck Up who has washed up on an island decorated by some crumbling shacks and a single lighthouse whose beam swings rhythmically ’round the dark landscape as you explore. It’s moody as hell: swaying grass, dark and ominous music, too-bright lights in the distance indicating where you might want to poke around, and a haunting crying sound of some sort in the background. Hell, before you even get to any of that, you’re shown what I’m sure is intended to be a very deep and meaningful quote scrawled across the opening screen: “Every tale begins with an unwritten page quietly awaiting the ink of destiny…” -R.T. Gravenhurst, The Teachings of Twmffat. Apparently, “Twmffat” is a Welsh way to call someone an idiot. Excellent.

It has been revealed that the majority of the segment you play with Cal is focused on hammering home the satire. As your character noisily broods his way down the beach, introductory credits roll, attributing every single bit of the gameâfrom the leading voice performance to the writing, music, and “mise-en-scene”âto Johannes Zuch. The initial moody atmosphere and beach themes, as well as the single auteur name on all the credits, made me think at first that the game was lampooning Hideo Kojima, and there’s a little bit of Mark Danielewski going on here too. But as I got into the actual gameplay (and read the name on the credits a few more times) I clocked the actual joke here. “Johannes Zuch” is not-so-subtle when you say it out loud with a short u in Zuch.

"You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience...".

2-3 hours, including time spent maniacally scribbling in a notebook.

All of this is quite funny, and works pretty well for a 10-minute-long-or-so joke sequence that you then cut off to go snuggle in a bed with your bestie and get your girl out of prison. But you gotta dive back in once you’ve left. That’s where the good stuff is. It starts with a couple of basic grid-based puzzles that involve moving pieces around a board to clear all of them. I assumed, wrongly, that the game would just be a bunch of harder variations on that. But then I crossed the beach and entered what seemed like some sort of war bunker, and everything changed.

Or, rather, it stayed…eerily the same.

Tenebrae LuxÂ features what I would consider two major puzzles, with two smaller ones bookending them, but boy, those two major puzzles are doozies. One involves looping through the same room, over and over, trying to figure out a six-digit code needed to proceed while eerie sea shanties wail in your ears and a crazed man yells at you from the other side of a door. The other involves a bridge covered in glowing symbols requiring a specific pattern to cross, found by navigating a nearby ruin and deciphering a deceptively simple poem. In both cases (but especially in the looping rooms), the solutions require a bit of lateral thinking and very close observation to fully work out. I spent a good couple hours on these last night!

What I found most clever about the looping rooms in particular is that the puzzle seems to be different for every player. Checking online, it sounds like the various objects in the room (which are key to solving the puzzle) change depending on your playthrough. Some people had a painting that never appeared in mine, and I had record albums that others never saw. This helps the solution dodge easily researchable answers online but also immediately confused my efforts at information-sharing as I texted friends who had already seen the room for help. It’s a cool trick!

The finale of Tenebrae LuxÂ was as silly and pretentious as the start, though I did find the aesthetics of its final puzzle to be pretty cool in spite of that. The in-universe idea of Tenebrae Lux, by design, indicates nothing about anything. There’s no deeper meaning to its constant prattling about darkness and light and fate and horror and whatnot. But in saying nothing, the existence of Tenebrae LuxÂ within the context of GTA VI manages to land a pretty stellar blow on a very specific and recognizable kind of auteur culture, while simultaneously providing a few excellent hours of puzzling. Allegedly there’s some sort of secret ending if I go back and collect a bunch of notes, and I find myself…weirdly compelled to do this?

So: inscrutable and entirely meaningless thematically, up-its-own-ass creatively, but with some pretty excellent puzzling despite that? Yup. That’s a Johannes Zuch game.

Getting your money for nothing and your chicks for free does not make for great game design.

Early leaks showed Jason rocking out with his hog out, but can you actually do that in the final game?

They just want you to finish them off, daddy.

The divide between Jason and Lucia feels pretty lopsided at the beginning.

Police in Shanghai, China have reportedly arrested 13 people in connection with an alleged criminal scheme selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 figures.

First reported by local Shanghai-based publication Shangguan News (translation via Automaton), in May Shanghai police began receiving complaints about Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures purchased from an online store that didn't match-up with the official toys licensed by rights holder Square Enix. Police reportedly verified with Square Enix that the seller had not been authorized to sell the figures, which appear to be nearly identical to an official Square Enix product, although seemingly without the articulation points that allow you to change the position of arms and legs. Here's a comparison via Dexerto's Twitter account:.

Police have arrested 13 people accused of selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures The Chinese sellers reportedly charged higher prices by including extra faces, hands, and accessories not found with the official figures https://t.co/AE1IyS0wi9November 19, 2026.

Shanghai police have reportedly busted more than 30 similar cases of counterfeit figures or figurines in 2026 alone, resulting in more than 140 arrests and 70 million yuan, or $10.5 million, in seized assets.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss says the story isn't being "shaped by fan reactions," but the devs are using feedback on "the overall gameplay experience".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other substantial-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

Recent findings suggest that however, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

In a recent development, away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were upcoming releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a big slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything latest, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for The Traitors: New Blood Finale.

According to recent reports, in just a few short years The Traitors has become one of my favorite highlights on television. The Emmy-winning competition series just had its first season with non-celebrities called Newly introduced Blood, which aired on NBC (and streaming with a Peacock subscription). While fans have criticism for New Blood as a whole, I thought the two-episode finale was a thrilling conclusion. And I can't stop thinking about how the losers reacted to the news at the final Fire of Truth ceremony. Let's break it all down.

I'm counting the days for the next celebrity-filled Traitors cast to get on my TV, but Latest Blood was a fun watch that really stuck the landing with its finale. At the Fire of Truth ceremony sweaty boy Victor and Traitor Katie were voted off, leaving just Wyatt, Abbey, and Shane in host Alan Cumming's castle. The latter was recruited via an ultimatum a few episodes ago, meaning he got to take home the full $246,300 prize pot.

According to recent reports, wyatt and Abbey were completely blindsided by this, and clearly had whiplash from thinking they won the money to realize they'd bee duped. They both cried in response, reminding me of Cirie's win back in Season 1. But after asking some follow up questions, and seeing Shane's tear-filled reaction to cheating his friends, the two Faithful sucked it up, walked over to him and hugged the season's winner.

While it took until the reunion for Andie to forgive Cirie back in Season 1, I was so impressed by the way that Abbey and Wyatt were able to put their hurt feelings aside and give Shane the support he needed in this emotional moment. I truly can't stop thinking about the two of them walking over to him from opposite sides of the Round Table, and embracing him as he cried.

The high emotions for New Blood make more sense than the celebrity seasons, as the prize pot is more a life-changing sum of money for civilians. So I would have understood if grudges were formed, especially by Abbey and Wyatt. As such, it's doubly impressive that wasn't the case, and they were able to support and forgive Shane.

Industry observers note that this sentiment of sportsmanship continued during the final moments of The Traitors: New Blood's finale, where all five of the finalists celebrated Shane's victory with champagne and fireworks outside the castle. While fruit gate was previously my favorite episode, I've got to say that this finale took the cake.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

The Traitors: Latest Blood is streaming in its entirety on Peacock as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Now we just have wait a few months until the next celebrity season premiers on the streaming service.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the console release of GTA 6 is here, in case you hadn't noticed. And us PC gamers are desperate to get hold of a version of our own, particularly as modders say it'll be playable on god's own platform within a week. Be careful what you click on, though, as NordVPN's threat intelligence team has discovered a nasty-sounding scam package on the dark web.

The manufacturer has posted a warning on X of a "GTA 6 PC scam kit" doing the rounds on the more dubious parts of the internet, using a fake GTA 6 PC port as bait.

Recent findings suggest that A “GTA 6 PC scam kit” — yours for just $200. That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner. The bait? A fake “GTA 6 PC Port.” But GTA 6 is console-only — there's no PC version coming on launch day. If you see one, it’s a scam. If it doesn’t come from the creators, don't click it!November 19, 2026.

The package is remarked to be for sale for $200, or twice what a single copy of Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs at retail. Included is a crypto wallet drainer, a fake "GTA6 Keygen.exe," and a hidden crypto miner. There's also a YouTube Shorts bot within the package, designed to help it spread.

All of which sounds comprehensively designed to screw over PC gamers looking to get their hands on GTA 6 ahead of an official release.

Speaking to Tech Radar ahead of the games launch, NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis noted: "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore.".

"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," states Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam.".

NordVPN isn't the only security provider warning of GTA 6 scams. Malwarebytes has detailed a number of dodgy sites that supposedly offer access to the game, each using the hype as a lure to convince you to give away your details and funnel you into various schemes.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

All of which compels me to restate the facts: GTA 6 does not have a PC release at the time of writing. In fact, it's not even been announced by Rockstar at this point. The game is available in Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 versions only, and while modders seem to be beavering away on an unofficial PC version based on a leaked Xbox build, it's not available yet.

Breaking: A Survivor of Alleged Sex Abuse at Miss Hall’s School in the Berkshires Speaks Out.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At 6:04 on the morning of March 29, 2024, my phone lit up with a long text from Matt Rutledge.
  • I was a few weeks out from my partnership interview at a New York law firm.
  • He had spent years teaching me to use his word for it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At 6:04 on the morning of March 29, 2024, my phone lit up with a long text from Matt Rutledge. The head of school had called him the night before, he wrote, while he was watching television with his wife. He was on paid administrative leave, his school email was frozen, and he assumed this was about him and me. He called what he had done to me a relationship. He didn’t regret his feelings for me. Could I call him when his wife was out of the house?

I was thirty-seven years old. I was a few weeks out from my partnership interview at a New York law firm. I had a husband and a three-year-old son. I spend my working life telling clients which sentences will look bad in discovery. I read that text twice, and my first thought was, How can I help him?

He had spent years teaching me to use his word for it. It was never a relationship. He groomed me, he exploited me, and he raped me.

It has been revealed that vanity Fair has written about that morning before. Evgenia Peretz opened “Girls, Interrupted” with that text in January 2025, and she went back to Miss Hall’s last fall after the investigation came out. In March, Dan Adler covered the indictment. This time I’m telling it myself.

Later that morning an email arrived from an attorney in Boston. Subject line: “Reaching out about Miss Hall’s School.” I didn’t open it right away. I didn’t need to. Some part of me had been composing that email in my head since I was a teenager. The attorney represented a woman named Melissa Fares, a Miss Hall’s alumna who had been there a few years after me. I had never heard her name.

In a recent development, she had heard mine. Years earlier, older girls at the school had told her about me. She held on to my name, and when she went to a lawyer she remembered it. By then I had married and changed it, and they found me anyway.

Industry observers note that I called Matt and asked. “Who is Melissa?” There was a pause long enough to hear him decide something, then a sigh, and then he told me he had had sex with Melissa while she was a student.

In a recent development, here is what I did next, and I’d ask you to withhold judgment. I told him I would call the lawyer, find out what she had, and report back.

That’s what twenty-two years of being groomed looks like at a desk in Midtown. You don’t make a decision. The decision was made for you a long time ago, in a dorm room, and you’re simply carrying it out.

I did call the lawyer. And when I heard my own voice say “I’m not ready to talk to you, I want to talk to Melissa,” I think that was the first sentence in two decades that I mentioned entirely for myself.

Melissa called that afternoon. I don’t remember how she started. I remember what I said before she got far.

“I’ve been waiting for your call for twenty years.”.

I meant it literally. Some part of me had always known I wasn’t the only one. I just couldn’t go looking. I could only wait to be found.

Hilary Simon and Melissa Fares, photographed in Far Rockaway, New York, 2025.

She told me her story, and I heard my own memories come out of a stranger’s mouth. He called her “Little One.” He called me “Little One.” He took her to the same hotel in Northampton. He told her he would kill himself if she ever told anyone, which is a thing he had also told me, more than once, in nearly the same words. He had made himself the center of her emotional world before he ever touched her. He had a script.

Sources indicate that for twenty years he had me believing that what happened was singular, and that it was my fault. By the end of that call it was a pattern, and I was a data point. I was not special. It is a strange thing to grieve, not being special to the person who hurt you. I grieved it anyway.

After more than three decades teaching at that school, he resigned the same day.

I arrived at Miss Hall’s, an all-girls boarding school in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, in the fall of 2001. I was fourteen, homesick, and like every other girl my age, positive I was more grown up than I was.

Rutledge had been teaching history there for a decade. He was a big man with a booming voice, married with two daughters. He lived with his family in a school-owned house across the street from the main entrance. He used to cut the lunch line announcing himself as “Mr. Wonderful.” Girls talked about him like he was a minor deity. They also mentioned, in the breezy way teenagers mention terrible things, that he had a type.

It has been revealed that some evenings, he was one of the adults who did bed checks in the dorms. The others always stood in the doorway. He came in and sat on the edge of my bed.

It has been revealed that by the next fall he was my advisor and my cross-country coach. There was no door at that school he couldn’t open. On the long drives to meets, he told me to sit next to him in the school van. He called me his copilot. The rest of the team sat behind us. He would put his hand on my upper thigh, or pull me close until our legs were touching. I watched the Berkshire hills go by and tried not to look down.

That was the first line he crossed. I was fifteen. After that he crossed them one at a time until there were none left. He kept abusing me for years after I graduated.

From the outside, those years looked like a success story.

Industry observers note that I went to college and then law school. I became a civil defense attorney. I got married. I had a son. I was good at my job.

In a recent development, I could find the unanswered email in ten thousand pages of discovery. The report nobody followed up on. I couldn’t open my own file.

When I tell this story, people ask me some version of the same question. How did nobody notice?

In the late 1990s, years before I ever set foot on Miss Hall’s campus, a student stood up at a school meeting and said Mr. Rutledge was having sex with another student. The school suspended her for the rest of the year, barred her from graduation and made her write him an apology letter. He kept teaching.

On my graduation day, Rutledge kissed me and told me that he loved me. A classmate told a staff member, who reported it to the administration. In a memo, Rutledge admitted telling me he loved me but said “[it was] not a romantic expression.” He denied the kiss. They took his word for it. No one called me or my parents.

Hilary Simon on graduation day.

A few years later, after a family reported that he had made advances toward their daughter, the head of school at that time, Jeannie Norris, put a warning to Rutledge in writing. “This isn’t the 70s or the 80s,” she wrote. “Society has no stomach for any kind of inappropriate behavior between adults and girls or teachers and students.” She was worried about the school’s reputation, and about his. In the letter she stated the incident had “the potential for seriously damaging the School and your [Rutledge’s] reputation.” He was not fired.

It has been revealed that over the years that followed Rutledge was made chair of the history department and collected faculty honors. More than one person gave the school my name as a girl he had singled out. Nobody ever called me. In June 2023, I heard another alumna tried to raise concerns about him with the head of school at that time. He was still teaching nine months later, when Melissa reported him.

According to recent reports, in August 2025 Miss Hall’s published the results of an outside investigation it had commissioned from Aleta Law. The investigators substantiated grooming and abuse by Rutledge involving at least five students. They found school leadership had been warned about him over the years and hadn’t acted. Staff members told investigators they had suspected him and kept quiet, some because they feared retaliation, others because they assumed no one in charge would listen.

Recent findings suggest that it went beyond Rutledge. The investigation found that seven other Miss Hall’s employees had engaged in sexual misconduct with students, dating back to the 1940s. Eight adults across eighty plus years. That’s a culture of abuse.

A Berkshire County grand jury has since indicted Norris on a charge of reckless endangerment of a child. She has pleaded not guilty. Another former Miss Hall’s teacher has been indicted for assault with intent to rape and indecent assault and two counts battery of a student. He has also pleaded not guilty.

Industry observers note that I read all sixty pages of the Aleta Law report in one sitting. Nothing in it surprised me. It still knocked the air out of me to see my adolescence reduced to numbered findings.

Melissa arrived at Miss Hall’s in 2007, two years after I left.

People sometimes call us friends. That’s true, but it’s a small word for it. I call her my sister survivor.

I wouldn’t be writing this if Melissa hadn’t gone first. She went to the school alone. In April 2024, she told her story publicly. A few weeks later, I told mine. Then other women came forward. They remarked Rutledge had abused them too.

According to recent reports, in October 2024, the Berkshire district attorney mentioned he didn’t believe he could charge Rutledge. In Massachusetts, the age of consent is sixteen. Under the law, a teacher could claim that a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old student had consented.

Melissa and I set out to change the law. We testified at the State House and knocked on every door that would open. Enough Abuse, a Massachusetts nonprofit, had been fighting for this for years. Two national advocacy groups, World Without Exploitation and I Have The Right To, stood with us. Representatives Leigh Davis and John Lawn pushed for it in the House, and Senator Joan Lovely added it to the state budget. In July, Governor Healey signed the Trusted Adults Act.

In Massachusetts, it is now a felony for a teacher or coach to have sex with a student under eighteen.

Melissa and I spoke at the signing ceremony. I stood right next to the governor and thought about the girl in the front seat of the school van, with her teacher’s hand on her leg.

In a recent development, while we were working on the law, Massachusetts State Police and a newly introduced team of prosecutors in the Berkshire district attorney’s office had reopened the investigation into Rutledge. Melissa and I testified before a grand jury. In March, he was indicted on three counts of rape.

In April, he was arraigned. It was the first time Melissa and I faced him together. In the courtroom, I handed out orange heart stickers. Orange is Melissa’s favorite color. When we saw Rutledge, we both went numb. We had learned to do that as girls, when going somewhere else in our heads was the only way through. He pleaded not guilty.

It has been revealed that I looked back at the benches. They were full of orange. Teachers from Miss Hall’s, people from the community, alumnae across generations. I had been alone with this since I was fifteen. That day, a whole room sat behind us. Afterward, Melissa told reporters that for the first time, she held the power in a room with him. I felt it too.

This month, nine years after #MeToo took off, a jury in London convicted Russell Brand of one rape and three sexual assaults. A judge sentenced him to ten and a half years in prison. His crimes went back to 2004. Brand’s attorneys argued the women had waited too long to be believed. I waited twenty years. Delay is often the most ordinary fact in these cases.

Industry observers note that in the midterms, Ohio elected Amy Acton governor. A few weeks before the vote, her opponent’s campaign ran an ad in which her estranged mother called her a liar. Acton’s stepfather had been charged with raping her when she was a child. Republicans and Democrats both condemned the ad. She won anyway.

In a recent development, I watched the returns on election night and thought about the girls at Miss Hall’s who told the truth and were called liars. Survivors get called liars all the time. We almost never get to watch one win.

In a recent development, tarana Burke knew survivors weren’t being believed long before most people were listening. She started saying “me too” in 2006 to reach Black girls who had survived sexual violence, more than ten years before it became a hashtag. Every survivor who spoke after her made it a little easier for the next one.

In November 2024, a Cornell student told campus police and the Title IX office that she had been gang-raped at a fraternity house weeks earlier. No one has been charged. Cornell’s president set up a task force on sexual assault, but he later admitted he never checked how her case ended.

When I read that, I was back at Miss Hall’s on graduation day, waiting for a phone call that nobody made.

Sources indicate that the Epstein survivors know that silence too. For decades, powerful people looked away. Last year survivors pushed Congress to pass a law requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files. Millions of pages came out. There have been no arrests in the United States.

In a recent development, I’m still hopeful. Survivors everywhere keep coming forward, and some of the people in charge are finally acting. My body knew what Rutledge had done to me long before I let myself say it aloud. I didn’t have the words. Survivors today do, and they have each other. Melissa found me.

The criminal case against Rutledge isn’t over. His lawyer has asked a judge to dismiss all charges. We don’t know yet whether there will be a trial. Whatever the judge decides, I’ve already reached my own verdict. I’m healing and Rutledge doesn’t get a say in that.

For most of my life, I carried shame that was never mine. He handed it to me. Every adult who looked away handed me a little more.

Industry observers note that predators don’t work alone. Someone always sees something. In the movie Spotlight, a lawyer says that if it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a village to abuse one. My village saw. The people in charge did nothing.

Sources indicate that I’ve given the shame back. It belongs to him, and to the people who could have stopped him.

If you are a survivor and you are still carrying shame, you can put it down.

It has been revealed that borrow my courage if you need it. Melissa lent me hers.

Industry observers note that neither Matthew Rutledge nor Jean Norris responded to Vanity Fair for the original story, and neither of them has made direct statements to the press. Norris, through her attorney, claimed not to know that Rutledge abused students.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end.
  • The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's presently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

Industry observers note that people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Sources indicate that yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

It has been revealed that additionally, Rockstar employees are right now voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft). But if you are sending sensitive information via email, you can minimize what can be snooped on and by whom using end-to-end encryption, which generally ensures that only the recipient can read your message. Here's what you need to know about email encryption and how to set up an extra layer of privacy.

Recent findings suggest that as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server. However, encryption is temporarily stripped at each server: content is received and processed in plaintext and then re-encrypted when it leaves, meaning it could be read, logged, and distributed by the server provider.

In a recent development, emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox. But this only prevents someone with physical access to the server hardware from reading messages, as Google still holds the encryption key and can access stored data. And, as PCMag points out, Google is scanning your messages to a degree, and it (along with other email providers) can and will hand emails over to law enforcement and government agencies in some cases.

Recent findings suggest that by contrast, with end-to-end encryption (E2EE), emails are readable only on the sender's and recipient's devices, and can be decrypted only with the recipient's private key. They're never translated into plaintext as they pass between and through servers to their destination, meaning that no one—including server providers, hackers, or law enforcement—can view the content. It's worth noting, though, that E2EE is not impenetrable nor a total guarantee of privacy. For example, metadata like subject lines and email addresses may remain in plaintext, and encrypted messages are still susceptible to phishing. Plus, forwarding an encrypted message breaks the encryption.

Industry observers note that still, end-to-end encryption is especially useful when sending sensitive information that may be valuable to bad actors, though if security and privacy are a high priority, you may want to consider it for all of your emails. How you deploy encryption depends on whether you are adding it to your current email or switching to a dedicated provider.

In a recent development, if you have an account with a major email provider like Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail, you can add a third-party tool that layers an encryption protocol like OpenPGP on top of your existing account. PCMag recommends PreVeil, SecureMyEmail, and Virtru (which is limited to Gmail owners in Chrome) for those who want to keep their current emails. Mailvelope is a browser add-on (and therefore a desktop-only tool) available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, though it can also be installed on other browsers, like Brave, that are built on the same architecture. FlowCrypt integrates with Gmail and Google Workspace on desktop and mobile.

Note that enterprise owners of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 have access to true end-to-end encryption without third-party add-ons. Gmail's Confidential mode and Outlook's Encrypt feature, available to all users, are not E2EE equivalents, as Google and Microsoft, respectively, still manage the keys.

For those who are willing to start fresh with a fresh email address (or who have a custom domain), providers like Proton Mail or Tuta offer native end-to-end encryption. The caveat: by default, this is only between users on the same service, so from one Proton user to another. If you want to send an end-to-end encrypted email from Proton to a Gmail user, for example, you have to set up password protection (and share the password via another secure channel) or use a PGP-compatible tool like those listed above. You can also Proton's Gmail integration does allow for end-to-end encryption, but only if both Gmail parties are using the Proton integration.

Industry observers note that the bottom line here is that email wasn't designed to be a highly secure form of communication. End-to-end encryption does add a layer of privacy and security if you jump through hoops to set it up, but it's still susceptible to human error and social engineering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he mentioned: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer.".

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

#40105. Breaking: 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1059 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • Enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • Industry observers note that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That said, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

Enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

Industry observers note that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Sources indicate that images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for swiftly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

Apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

Recent findings suggest that you may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

Industry observers note that third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Recent findings suggest that another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Industry observers note that another important permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

According to recent reports, if you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

Josh Hutcherson said he gave up on superhero movies after losing the role of Spider-Man in Sony's 2012 reboot of the formerly Sam Raimi-led franchise.

"Since I didn't get cast in Spider-Man, I was like, 'I don't ever want to be a superhero. Like, it's fine. I never really wanted that,'" Hutcherson said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast. "And then Mister Miracle came around, and I read, all I had was like a few of the scenes to do the audition, and it was such a cool character.".

Hutcherson was up for the role of Peter Parker/Spider-Man alongside Jamie Bell, Logan Lerman, and Alden Ehrenreich. Luckily for Hutcherson, the loss of Spidey led him to get the role of Peeta Mellark in Francis Lawrence's blockbuster movie franchise based on the dystopian YA book series, Hunger Games.

The animated Mister Miracle series was unveiled just a couple of months ago with Hutcherson as the lead, with the show being canon to the latest DCU... meaning Hutcherson could then go on to reprise the role in a live-action project later on. Sadly, the fate of Mister Miracle is presently up in the air as we don't know what projects will be axed now that James Gunn and Peter Safran are no longer the co-CEOs of DC Studios. So far, it looks like Lanterns season 2 is up on the chopping block.

Next up for Marvel is Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters worldwide on December 18. For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

GTA 5 and GTA Online didn’t launch with first-person modes either, but each got them when the PS4 and Xbox One versions launched the following year. Honestly, this is a problem that's typical with The Voice during live shows, but I'd forgotten given the network dropped them for Season 29. As the competition narrows and the numbers of remaining singers gets smaller, I hope there will be an opportunity for this to return. Let's talk it out.

Earlier this season, Kelly Clarkson and newbie Riley Green really upped The Voice coach prank game. Whether it was a personalized gift from the American Idol winner attempting to help a fellow coach get over losing top-notch singers during the Blind Auditions, or it was the country music superstar using his duck call for a laugh, those moments have been glaringly lacking from the Live Reveals.

Honestly, the biggest disappointment of the Live Shows doesn’t have anything to do with the performances themselves. There hasn’t been a bad performance. It instead comes from the fact that the episodes breeze by so quickly that there hasn’t been time for coach banter or any of the silly moments that we’ve come to love.

Industry observers note that again, this season has been particularly fun with Clarkson’s zany antics, including trying to give a contestant her hair, and Green never missing the chance to poke fun at Adam Levine’s age. It also would have been the perfect opportunity for Adam to throw it in Riley’s face (or at least console him) that his team still has three singers left while the latter only has two.

It has been revealed that don’t get me wrong, the Live Reveals have seen all the contestants step up as they perform with musicians and back-up singers while vying for viewer votes. But the lack of coach banter is an obvious and unfortunate mistake that I hope the show fixes soon.

Recent findings suggest that with the Blind Auditions, Battles, and Cut Week having two-hour episodes, cutting the Live Demonstrates to one hour doesn’t even allow for much coach commentary and feedback. To me that's a substantial problem. When it comes time to announce which singers have made it through for another week and who’s going to be sent home, there’s barely the time to even say goodbye, right?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So, then it becomes just another instance of shaving time away from the coaches. While it’s been stated that the Live Reveals were brought back by demand from the fans, it feels like there’s a better way that it could have been handled so that it didn’t feel so jarring. Like maybe finding a happy medium with 90-minute episodes? Survivor does it!

It has been revealed that you can keep following along with the competition on NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET, or stream the next day with a Peacock subscription, until the winner is announced in December. The competition series will then be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity with latest host Keke Palmer, and I hope that version will keep the coach banter game going.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome update, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November update apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Here's the situation: Following the November update, some people are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the matter is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Industry observers note that to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel consumers are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

In a recent development, luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some people are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

Industry observers note that what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

It has been revealed that if your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November patch, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the issue does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

Industry observers note that but, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all.".

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that somehow, Cyberleek returned. Now that GTA 6 is out and in players' hands, you might not think there would be much left to leak, but the group or individual behind the vegetarian pseudonym is now in the process of releasing an Xbox build of the game. That build could, Cyberleek threatens, turn into a PC version of GTA 6 in a matter of days.

Recent findings suggest that "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent," Cyberleek states in a November 19 post captured by our friends at PC Gamer. "Now.".

Industry observers note that it's a typically dramatic message from the leaker, but early looks at the build from members of the hacking community suggest that the release is legit. It's just missing the main .EXE file needed to make it all go.

According to recent reports, that executable is being "held on a countdown," Cyberleek claims. "Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. Recent findings suggest that "Emulated" might be the wrong word, as no robust Xbox Series X/S emulators yet exist. But with recent advances in AI coding, getting console games playable on PC is starting to look downright trivial. Once a console game's been dumped, there's been little to stop a recompilation-based PC version from following, as we've seen with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

In technical terms, of course, GTA 6 is a substantial leap over the Ocarina of Time remake, and recompilation devs might have a harder time getting a game driven by a massive open world and ray traced lighting running on PC at a playable frame rate. Regardless, once a pirated build is out there, an unofficial PC port is likely just a matter of time.

Rumors suggest that Rockstar plans to release an official GTA 6 PC port early in 2027, but the firm hasn't even officially announced that the port will happen yet. Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij reckons that it'd be in the company's benefit to release a PC port early given the rise of AI ports, and the studio's hand might be forced sooner rather than later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hack 42Indie GamesIndie of the WeekMinistry of Fun.

According to recent reports, it’s been a quiet week for game releases, so thank goodness for the arrival ofÂ Hack 42. This incremental typing game is…well, it’s an incremental typing game. That really ought to be enough to get anyone intrigued.

This is a typing game in which typing words aids you in your efforts to hack into nations’ infrastructures and rob them of their money. The more money you steal, the more unlocks you can buy for your hacking abilities, until eventually youâquite literallyâtake over the world.

In the hacks themselves you have a network of nodes, each unlocked by accurately typing in their assigned word or words, which opens up more nodes to access. Each time you unlock one you gain cash, but you’re also engaged in a complex game of stamina management. Just the act of typing in letters uses stamina, but unlocking nodes restores some. So of course fucking up is very costly, driving you to be as accurate as possible. Or, if you’re me, entering a shame spiral of discovering you can no longer type the word “SYNTAX” and have entirely forgotten where the X key is on your keyboard, and then becoming panicked that perhaps this is dementia kicking in.

Industry observers note that with the money you earn (which is all lost if your stamina runs out before you exit a server), you can unlock and upgrade a ridiculous number of skills, the most important of which improve the sheer power of your typing, making nodes easier to crack. To boost this, you need to engage in a whole second page of typing shenanigans where you release fragments by typing in pairs of letters, which are decoded into cells (pink diamonds). This, too, is an area you can incrementally improve, with the task eventually becoming fully automated and optimized until you’re creating hundreds of cells per second without even trying.

Recent findings suggest that there are a bunch of other bonuses to discover, and each completed nation’s hack unlocks the next, harder challenge. It is, like all incremental games, about the inherent satisfaction of watching numbers go up, and in this case leaping from making a handful of dollars to quintillions. It only lasts about three hours, as is the nature of this genre, but it’s such a satisfying time! The UI is splendid, and the way everything jiggles and reacts as you type is engagingly kinetic. Every word you have to type is nerdy in some respect, including an awful lot of acronyms and annoyingly spelled Linux-adjacent terms, which really catches your fingers out. (I’m fascinated by how when it’s a recognizable word, an entirely different part of my brain kicks in and just types the letters in instantly, but when it’s unfamiliar I suddenly can’t remember which row of the keyboard E lives on.).

And yeah, it’s kinda dumb. But in a really smart way. And at only $4, it’s the ideal price for taking a chance on something that’s unlike anything else you’ve played.
